query: For a multi-principal element alloy system known for limited ductility in cast forms, propose a processing route and phase constitution that would simultaneously achieve nanocrystalline grain sizes below 50 nm and a dual-phase solid solution structure, thereby enhancing hardness and yield strength without inducing brittle intermetallic formation. Support this hypothesis with prior evidence regarding grain refinement mechanisms and phase stability limits, define the boundary conditions where this microstructure becomes unstable, and suggest a falsification experiment to distinguish this mechanism from simple solid solution strengthening.

generation.hypothesis: A multi-principal element alloy system can achieve nanocrystalline grain sizes below 50 nm and a dual-phase solid solution structure through a processing route that involves severe plastic deformation and subsequent heat treatment, thereby enhancing hardness and yield strength without inducing brittle intermetallic formation.
generation.intervention: Severe plastic deformation and heat treatment
generation.mechanism: Phase stability limits and solid solution strengthening
generation.uncertainty: Phase stability limits and grain refinement mechanisms are not well understood
generation.falsification_experiment: Compare the mechanical properties of the alloy system with and without severe plastic deformation and heat treatment
